properties.name: Hadrian acclaimed emperor at Antioch
properties.one_line: The legions at Antioch proclaimed Hadrian emperor on 11 August, the exact day this map is set — news of Trajan's death two days earlier having just reached the city.

properties.name: Kitos War — Cyrenaica revolt
properties.one_line: Jewish rebels under Lukuas devastated Cyrenaica so thoroughly that Hadrian later had to send fresh colonists to resettle the depopulated province.

properties.name: Kitos War — Egypt suppression
properties.one_line: Marcius Turbo's combined land and naval force retook Alexandria from Lukuas's rebels and pacified the Egyptian countryside by autumn 117.

properties.name: Kitos War — Cyprus revolt at Salamis
properties.one_line: Jewish rebels under Artemion razed Salamis, the provincial capital of Cyprus, prompting Rome to ban Jews from the island afterward, even shipwreck survivors.

properties.name: Kitos War — Mesopotamia and Babylonia revolt
properties.one_line: Jewish communities across newly-conquered Mesopotamia rose against Rome in the rear of Trajan's Parthian campaign, and were suppressed by Lusius Quietus before he moved on to Judaea.

properties.name: Siege of Lydda
properties.one_line: Lusius Quietus besieged the Judaean town of Lydda, where rebels had gathered under Julianus and Pappus and Rabban Gamaliel II was trapped inside.

properties.name: Execution of the Martyrs of Lydda
properties.one_line: Rebel leaders Julianus and Pappus were captured and executed at Lydda, remembered afterward in rabbinic sources as the "slain of Lydda."

properties.name: Trajan captures Ctesiphon
properties.one_line: Trajan took the Parthian capital Ctesiphon in 116, briefly installing a puppet king and forming the short-lived province of Mesopotamia.

properties.name: Parthian War — Roman position collapses
properties.one_line: By 117 the failed siege of Hatra and renewed Parthian resistance had unraveled Trajan's conquests, and Rome's brief hold on Mesopotamia was already being abandoned as the emperor withdrew toward Syria.

properties.name: Colonia Ulpia Traiana Augusta Dacica Sarmizegetusa founded
properties.one_line: The new provincial capital of Dacia, built from scratch after the 106 conquest and named for Trajan, was by 117 a going colonia with forum, amphitheater, and governor's palace.

properties.name: Gold rush at Alburnus Maior
properties.one_line: Illyrian colonists worked Rome's new Dacian gold mines at Alburnus Maior, the wealth that had driven Trajan's two Dacian wars in the first place.

properties.name: Petra under Roman rule
properties.one_line: The former Nabataean royal capital lost its political status when Trajan annexed the kingdom in 106, though it remained the province's religious center.

properties.name: Bostra made capital of Arabia Petraea
properties.one_line: Trajan made Bostra the new capital and legionary base of the province of Arabia Petraea after annexing the Nabataean kingdom in 106.

properties.name: Trajan's Column dedicated
properties.one_line: The 30-meter marble column narrating the Dacian Wars in a spiraling relief was dedicated in Trajan's new forum on 12 May 113.

properties.name: Forum and Markets of Trajan dedicated
properties.one_line: Apollodorus of Damascus's vast new forum complex, funded by the spoils of the Dacian Wars, was dedicated in January 112 alongside its adjoining market halls.

properties.name: Aqua Traiana opened
properties.one_line: Trajan's new aqueduct began delivering spring water from Lake Bracciano, 57 kilometers away, into the Trastevere district and the Janiculum in 109.

properties.name: Antioch earthquake
properties.one_line: A massive earthquake leveled much of Antioch while Trajan was wintering there for the Parthian campaign, killing the consul Marcus Pedo Vergilianus and nearly the emperor himself.
